name: amigit
readme:
Short:        Local-only git client for AmigaOS 3.x
Type:         dev/misc
Architecture: m68k-amigaos >= 68020
Uploader:     duncan@bowring.us
Author:       Duncan Bowring (amiport, built on libgit2)
Version:      0.1-2
URL:          https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport

amigit -- Local-only git client for AmigaOS 3.x

An amiport-native git CLI built on libgit2 1.8.5. Local repositories
only; no network commands (no clone/fetch/push/pull/remote). Covers
the v1 ten-command core: version, init, status, log, show, diff,
add, commit, checkout, branch, tag. Upstream git is infeasible on
AmigaOS because its command dispatch is built on fork()/execvp(),
which AmigaOS does not provide; libgit2 is embedded directly into
the binary instead.

Project: https://github.com/bdgscotland/amiport
Built on: libgit2 1.8.5, zlib 1.3.1, amiport posix-shim

Cross-compiled with m68k-amigaos-gcc 6.5.0b for AmigaOS 3.x. Targets
68020 minimum (no 68000/A500 support -- accelerated Amigas only).
Tested in FS-UAE (Amiga 1200) with 82/82 functional tests passing.

What's new in 0.1-2:
  - Compiled with -m68020 (was -m68000). Faster on Vampire/68030/40
    accelerators. A500 with stock 68000 is no longer supported.
  - Friendly error when 'amigit init' is run with no positional
    arguments from a working directory whose volume name is more
    than one character (e.g. 'WORK:', 'Ram Disk:', 'System 3.1:').
    libgit2's internal path root recognizer only handles single-
    character drive letters; the multi-char volume case now exits
    with a helpful 'use: amigit init <path>' message instead of a
    cryptic libgit2 './.' error. All other commands (status, log,
    add, commit, etc.) work normally from any CWD.
  - cmd_log hot path uses fputs/fputc instead of printf, avoiding
    libnix's format-parser overhead when walking long histories.
  - amigit_is_help_flag() consolidated into a single shared helper
    -- removed 10 duplicate static definitions across cmd_*.c.
  - New positional-argument matrix test enforces zero-arg coverage
    (the 'amigit init in a Shell' case) so this regression cannot
    sneak back in. Test count: 82 (was 81).

Usage:
  amigit version                      Print version info
  amigit init [--bare] <path>         Create an empty repository
  amigit status [-s]                  Show worktree and index state
  amigit log [-n N]                   Walk HEAD's commit history
  amigit show <ref>                   Show a commit with its diff
  amigit diff [--cached]              Unified diff (worktree or staged)
  amigit add <path>...                Stage files into the index
  amigit commit -m <msg>              Record a commit (single-word msg)
  amigit checkout <ref>               Switch HEAD to a branch or tag
  amigit branch [-l] [-d] [name]      List/create/delete branches
  amigit tag [-l] [name]              List or create lightweight tags

Exit codes (Amiga-native):
  0  = success (RETURN_OK)
  10 = any error (RETURN_ERROR)
  20 = fatal (RETURN_FAIL)

Known limitations:
  - No network commands. clone/fetch/push/pull/remote/submodule
    require bsdsocket + libssh2/http-shim -- a future Phase 4.
  - No merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, or stash.
  - No interactive flows (add -i, rebase -i, commit --amend with
    editor). AmigaOS has no portable $EDITOR integration.
  - Commit messages via -m must be a single shell token; -F <file>
    (multi-line) is planned for 0.1-3.
  - 'amigit init' with no positional args produces a friendly error
    on multi-character volume names (libgit2 path-root limitation).
    Use 'amigit init <path>' instead.
  - No color output, no pager integration.

Binary: ~1.05 MB. Stack: 256 KB. Requires 4 MB free RAM at runtime.
porting_notes: First working git client for AmigaOS 3.x. Written from scratch as an amiport-native CLI on top of the pruned lib/libgit2/libgit2.a (1.8.5) because upstream git's fork()/execvp()-based command dispatch is structurally infeasible on 68k AmigaOS. Implements the PDR-010a v1 ten-command core: version, init, status, log, show, diff, add, commit, checkout, branch, tag. Two libgit2 path-handling quirks worked around at the port level (volume-rooted X:foo -> X:/foo rewrite in amigit_resolve_repo_path for single-letter volumes; multi-char volume CWD-init produces a friendly error pointing at the explicit-path workaround in 0.1-2). One FS-UAE-specific soft-float crash in libgit2's patch_generate.c worked around via __divsf3/__floatunsisf stubs in the port's link-time stubs file (crash-pattern #2: libnix mathieeesingbas ROM library broken on FS-UAE). 0.1-2 flips amigit to -m68020 (target audience is accelerated Amigas; A500/68000 dropped) -- HONEST disclosure: at -O0 the flag is essentially cosmetic for amigit's TUs, the real perf cliff is rebuilding lib/libgit2 at -m68020 which is deferred to 0.1-3. Also consolidates duplicated is_help_flag helpers and rewrites cmd_log's hot path to use fputs+fputc instead of printf (this one IS effective on libnix). 82/82 FS-UAE functional tests pass.
known_limitations: No network commands (clone/fetch/push/pull/remote) -- requires bsdsocket + libssh2 or http-shim in a future Phase 4. No merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, or stash. No interactive flows (rebase -i, add -i, commit --amend with editor). Commit messages via -m must be single shell tokens; -F <file> (multi-line from file) is planned for 0.1-3. 'amigit init' with no positional args produces a friendly error on multi-character volume names (libgit2 git_fs_path_root only recognizes single-character ASCII drive prefixes; use 'amigit init <path>' instead). No color output, no pager integration. Empty initial commits rejected (no --allow-empty). Requires 4 MB free RAM at runtime. 68020 minimum -- no plain 68000/A500 support.
